question: Which infection is famous for causing thick, white cottage-cheese discharge and intense itching?

question: Why is community-centred care considered a shift from traditional hospital nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any medications or clinical equipment
options.B: It focuses only on newborn babies and ignores elderly populations
options.C: It moves the focus from treating sickness in facilities to preventing illness in neighborhoods
options.D: It relies entirely on doctors rather than nurses to provide care

explanation: Traditional nursing often waits for patients to become sick enough to enter a hospital, whereas community-centred care proactively addresses health where people live. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: A staff nurse wants to move from a general ward into the busy Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Which benefit of continuing education makes this possible?

options.A: Reducing hospital expenses
options.B: Lowering patient admission rates
options.C: Promoting specialization
options.D: Simplifying medical records

explanation: Specialization gives you the exact skills and confidence you need to step into advanced areas like the ICU or theatre. You can grow your career step by step! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h2)

question: Why is foetal scalp blood sampling sometimes performed when a CTG is abnormal?

options.C: To stimulate the baby to move away from the umbilical cord
options.D: To collect a DNA sample for genetic screening after birth

question: What is the main focus of custodial care?

options.A: Performing emergency surgeries and acute trauma procedures
options.B: Administering complex intravenous medications and therapies
options.C: Providing non-medical help with daily living and personal needs
options.D: Curing acute infections through targeted antibiotic therapy

explanation: Custodial care is entirely non-medical and centers on helping people manage their routine daily needs rather than curing active diseases. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which common condition causes physical blockage and urinary retention in older men?

options.B: Glomerular nephritis
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: Urinary tract infection

question: A stroke patient has weak muscles and needs a little bit of help to move their arm fully. What exercise is best?

options.A: Active-assistive exercises
options.B: Passive range of motion
options.C: Complete bed rest restriction
options.D: Heavy weightlifting resistance

question: Why is a suspected hole (perforation) in the gut a major warning sign against using regular barium?

options.A: The X-ray machine cannot see through leaked barium
options.B: Barium leaks into the abdomen and causes severe inflammation
options.C: The barium will instantly dissolve in the bloodstream
options.D: It will cause immediate kidney failure

explanation: Think of it this way: if the gut has a hole, barium can leak out into the belly and cause a very dangerous reaction and infection. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: In young children with sickle cell anaemia, what is dactylitis?

options.A: Severe infection of the lung tissue
options.B: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.C: Sudden yellowing of the eyes and skin
options.D: Abnormal enlargement of the liver

explanation: Dactylitis is often one of the very first signs of sickle cell disease in babies. It happens when sickled cells block blood flow in the tiny bones of the hands and feet, causing painful swelling. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main goal of performing medication reconciliation?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital pharmacy supplies
options.B: To test the memory of newly graduated nursing students
options.C: To avoid errors like missed doses, double dosing, and clashes
options.D: To force patients to buy their medications from the hospital

explanation: The core purpose is to catch and stop mistakes early, keeping your patient safe from harmful drug clashes. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the biggest benefit of a psychologically safe work culture on the ward?

options.A: Employees never experience any form of physical fatigue or tiredness.
options.B: Patients are discharged from the hospital twice as fast.
options.C: Hospital operating costs are reduced to absolute zero immediately.
options.D: Staff feel comfortable reporting near-misses without fear of harsh punishment.

explanation: When people aren't terrified of being yelled at, they will speak up about close calls or mistakes. That open communication is what keeps patients truly safe! [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h4)

question: What happens when someone's line of gravity moves outside their base of support?

options.A: Muscle strength instantly doubles
options.B: Blood pressure drops to zero
options.C: Joint flexibility increases
options.D: The person loses balance and falls

explanation: Spot on! If your center of balance wanders outside your footing, gravity takes over and down you go. That's why wide stances keep us steady. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do nurses use a pH testing strip when checking a newly placed nasogastric tube?

options.A: To test how acidic the fluid pulled from the tube is

options.C: To check if the patient has a stomach ulcer
options.D: To measure the sugar level in the feed

explanation: Stomach acid is very sour! Testing the pH of fluid from the tube helps us confirm the tip is safely inside the acidic stomach, not the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h3)

question: When can a patient get pregnant again after a misoprostol medical abortion?

options.A: After six months for the uterus to heal
options.B: Never, because medical abortion causes permanent sterility
options.C: Immediately, as ovulation can resume before the next period
options.D: Only after waiting three normal menstrual cycles

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Ovulation can happen even before the very first post-abortion period arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h8)

question: Which food item is generally encouraged on a low protein meal plan?

options.A: Red meat
options.B: Dried beans
options.C: White rice
options.D: Whole wheat bread

question: A nurse washes her hands thoroughly with soap and water before entering a patient's room. Which group of germs is she mostly trying to wash away?

options.A: Resident microbiota
options.B: Systemic pathogens
options.C: Endogenous spores
options.D: Transient microbiota

explanation: Spot on! When you touch door handles or charts, you pick up temporary ('transient') microbes. Handwashing washes those casual hitchhikers right down the drain before you touch your patient. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

options.A: It represents the maximum depth of permanent skin and muscle destruction.
options.B: Infection rarely occurs in this specific layer of the burn wound.
options.C: This area is completely insensate and requires immediate surgical removal.
options.D: Tissue in this zone has reduced blood flow and can be saved from necrosis.

explanation: The zone of stasis is bruised and sluggish, but not dead yet! Quick fluids keep blood flowing there so it doesn't cross over into tissue death (necrosis). Great nursing care saves the day! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h1)

question: What do we mean when we talk about a drug's 'affinity'?

options.A: The time it takes for a drug to dissolve
options.B: The attraction between a drug and its receptor
options.C: The total amount of drug excreted in urine
options.D: The speed at which the liver metabolizes a drug

explanation: Affinity is basically how strongly a drug 'likes' and sticks to its specific receptor. High affinity means a tight, cozy fit! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h3)

question: A patient gets severe bloating and gas after drinking milk. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: High dietary protein intake
options.B: Lactose intolerance
options.C: Gastric acid hypersecretion
options.D: Excessive swallowed air

explanation: When someone lacks enough of the lactase enzyme, milk sugar goes undigested, and gut bacteria turn it into gas. Classic lactose intolerance! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which of these is a very common complaint from patients suffering from Long COVID?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin
options.B: Chronic fatigue and brain fog
options.C: Sudden bone fractures in the legs
options.D: Uncontrollable weight gain

explanation: You got it! Many people with Long COVID struggle with lingering tiredness and trouble concentrating, often called 'brain fog'. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of the thick mucus layer inside your stomach?

options.A: To protect the stomach tissue from its own acid and enzymes
options.B: To activate pepsinogen into working pepsin
options.C: To help move food quickly into the small intestine
options.D: To absorb vitamin B12 directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Since stomach acid is strong enough to break down food, that thick mucus layer acts like a shield so the stomach doesn't digest itself! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main job of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine when given during shock?

options.A: Dissolving blood clots inside blocked arteries
options.B: Dilating peripheral airways to ease breathing
options.C: Lowering heart rate to reduce cardiac workload
options.D: Constricting blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors squeeze ('press') the blood vessels, tightening up the pipes to raise the blood pressure and keep vital organs perfused when the patient's own pressure is tanking. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h7)

question: What is the main job of the upper oesophageal sphincter when you are just resting and not swallowing?

options.A: To stop gastric acid from reaching the pharynx
options.B: To prevent air from entering the digestive tract
options.C: To produce mucus for lubricating food boluses
options.D: To grind up large food particles before entry

explanation: Great thinking! By staying shut when we aren't eating, this sphincter keeps us from accidentally sucking air into our stomach every time we breathe in. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h5)

question: A male nurse with a thick beard is caring for a patient with TB. What should he do?

options.A: Shave his beard so the N95 can seal properly
options.B: Wear an N95 right over his beard
options.C: Wear a standard surgical mask instead
options.D: Double-mask with two surgical masks

question: Why is drying the newborn baby immediately after birth a critical nursing action?

options.C: To check for hidden birthmarks and bruises
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

question: How does the endocrine system compare to the nervous system when it comes to response time?

options.A: It relies exclusively on electrical nerve impulses
options.B: It produces slower, longer-lasting responses
options.C: It produces faster, short-lived responses
options.D: It only functions during times of acute physical trauma

explanation: While the nervous system acts like a quick text message (fast and brief), the endocrine system acts more like a long letter—it takes a bit longer to arrive, but the effect sticks around much longer! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h1)

question: Where do community health clients usually receive their care?

options.C: Inside locked psychiatric wards during involuntary confinement
options.D: Only within private surgical suites following major operations

question: A patient in the intensive care unit is being evaluated for potential brain death. Which test is routinely used to confirm this?

options.C: Barium swallow study
options.D: Electromyography

question: Which group is considered especially vulnerable in community health?

options.D: Licensed medical practitioners

question: Why should a patient avoid putting lotion on their residual limb before wearing a shrinker sock?

question: What does the SBAR acronym stand for during a patient handover?

options.D: Staff, Beds, Ambulances, Reports

question: A patient comes in with yellow eyes (sclera) and dark urine. What process is likely happening?

options.C: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells releasing bilirubin

question: Why shouldn't patients take erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) together with organic nitrates?

question: What is the main job of an antidote in poisoning cases?

options.D: A chemical that completely destroys red blood cells

question: What are the classic warning signs of phlebitis at an IV site?

question: What is one of the earliest psychological signs that a patient is entering shock?

question: A newly intubated patient has absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest and gurgling noises over the epigastrium when ventilated. What does this strongly suggest?

question: What is the main reason we do a bladder irrigation?

question: What is an important daily nursing task for a patient on continuous nasal cannula oxygen?

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning before discharging a post-abortion care patient?

question: What term describes the physical need for higher doses of a drug to get the same effect?

question: A family notices that their monthly income stays the same, but the cost of staple foods doubles due to inflation. What is this family most likely forced to do?

options.C: Buy cheaper, highly processed foods to stretch their tight budget
options.D: Automatically increase their daily consumption of fresh organic produce

question: What is the main job of the effector in a homeostatic loop?

question: Why do women who have undergone infibulation frequently suffer from recurrent urinary tract infections?

question: During peritoneal dialysis, what part of the patient's body acts as the natural filtering membrane?

options.C: The basement membrane of the remaining renal tubules
options.D: The semipermeable filter inside the hemodialysis machine

question: What is the main duty of the anaesthetist during an operation?

options.A: Monitoring the patient's vital signs and managing pain

options.C: Documenting sponge and instrument counts every thirty minutes
options.D: Handing sterile instruments directly to the operating surgeon

question: Why is it so dangerous to mix sleeping pills with alcohol?

options.C: It leads to profound respiratory depression and coma due to additive central nervous system suppression
options.D: It triggers severe high blood pressure and sudden stroke

question: Which attitude is most important for a nurse during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: Non-judgmental and empathetic
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Indifferent and detached
options.D: Strictly authoritative and firm

question: How does poor lighting contribute to home accidents?

options.D: It causes sudden dizziness and fainting spells

question: When assessing the tummy (abdomen), why must a nurse listen with a stethoscope *before* pressing or feeling around?

options.C: Auscultation warms up the stethoscope for the patient
options.D: Palpation causes immediate severe pain in all patients

question: What is the standard first-line oral antibiotic for treating non-severe pneumonia in under-fives?

options.D: Tetracycline

question: Why do doctors check uric acid levels when a patient complains of painful joints?

options.C: It rules out bacterial joint infections completely
options.D: It tracks the daily loss of calcium from the bones

question: What are diverticula?

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

question: Which finding is considered a normal, expected temporary side effect following a cystoscopy procedure?

options.B: Inability to feel the need to urinate for several weeks
options.C: Severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the shoulders

question: How do the kidneys balance out the mild breathing changes (respiratory alkalosis) that happen during pregnancy?

question: What is the correct way to store an epinephrine auto-injector?

question: Which needle gauge range is most appropriate for an intradermal injection?

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a telltale sign of bleeding in the gut (GI bleed), a serious side effect of long-term NSAID use. Always report this right away! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why do patients need X-rays or scans before starting cervical traction?

options.A: To prove the patient has health insurance
options.B: To find out the patient's favorite neck position
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the patient
options.D: To check for hidden bone weakness or instability

explanation: Imaging acts like a roadmap so the healthcare team can make sure there are no surprises like hidden fractures before applying traction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why are nurses often considered the central hub of the healthcare team?

options.A: They spend the most continuous time at the patient bedside
options.B: They make all the final diagnoses for hospital admissions
options.C: They hold the legal authority to hire and fire doctors
options.D: They control the entire hospital financial budget

explanation: That's right! Because nurses are right there by the bedside around the clock, we are usually the first to notice changes and connect all the other team members. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h4)

question: What does the term AEFI stand for in public health nursing?

options.A: Adverse Event Following Immunization
options.B: Acute Epidemic Fever Infection
options.C: Annual Evaluation of Facility Infrastructure
options.D: Assigned Emergency First-aid Intervention

explanation: AEFI is the standard global acronym used to describe medical incidents occurring after a person receives a vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: A young couple visits the clinic and mentions that multiple relatives on both sides died young from the same rare heart condition. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Prescribe blood pressure medication for both partners
options.B: Construct a pedigree chart and refer them for genetic assessment
options.C: Advise them to change their cooking oil immediately
options.D: Tell them not to worry because heart disease is completely normal

explanation: A pattern of early-onset disease in multiple relatives is a major red flag requiring formal genetic risk evaluation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: Which leadership style involves making all decisions alone and giving direct orders?

options.A: Laissez-faire
options.B: Democratic
options.C: Autocratic
options.D: Servant

explanation: An autocratic leader keeps full control of decision-making and expects strict compliance from the nursing staff. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which specific protein in the intestine makes Oral Rehydration Therapy work so well?

options.A: SGLT1
options.B: Gastric lipase
options.C: Potassium pump
options.D: Insulin receptor

explanation: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose linked transporter type 1) is the hero protein! It links sugar and salt uptake in the small intestine to pull precious water into the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h3)

question: In the fast AVPU neurological screening tool, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Responds to pain
options.B: Pulse is present
options.C: Patient is paralyzed
options.D: Pupils react

explanation: AVPU is a quick check: Alert, Verbal, Pain, Unresponsive. 'P' means the patient only wakes up or reacts when you apply pain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h4)

question: What does 'values clarification' help a nurse examine?

options.A: Hospital equipment inventory
options.B: Monthly salary deductions
options.C: Personal beliefs and biases
options.D: Public transport schedules

explanation: Values clarification is a great self-check tool. It allows us as nurses to look at our own inner biases so our personal opinions never get in the way of great patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: Which specialized skin cells make the pigment melanin?

options.A: Melanocytes
options.B: Fibroblasts
options.C: Langerhans cells
options.D: Keratinocytes

explanation: Correct! Melanocytes are the clever cells in our lower epidermis that produce melanin. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a physical problem caused by long-term, unmanaged stress?

options.A: Amplified perception of physical pain
options.B: Exacerbation of chronic hypertension
options.C: Improved gastrointestinal absorption of all nutrients
options.D: Delayed wound healing and tissue repair

explanation: Stress actually messes with digestion and reduces nutrient absorption—it definitely doesn't improve your gut health! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of using surgical safety checklists in the operating theatre?

options.A: To prevent communication breakdowns and critical errors
options.B: To slow down the surgical team so they do not get tired
options.C: To satisfy insurance companies so they pay higher fees
options.D: To calculate the total cost of surgical supplies used

explanation: Safety checklists ensure every team member verifies vital details like patient identity and procedure site before starting, reducing preventable errors. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the big advantage of using rapid molecular tests like GeneXpert for TB?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a thorough patient history.
options.B: They provide fast results and detect drug resistance early.
options.C: They can cure the infection without any medications.
options.D: They are completely painless and require no patient samples.

explanation: GeneXpert is fantastic because it gives results in just a few hours and tells us right away if the drugs won't work against that specific strain. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is a large-bore tube used for gastric lavage instead of a standard small feeding tube?

options.A: To make it easier for the nurse to push fluid deep into the small intestines
options.B: To ensure the fluid goes directly into the respiratory airway for safety
options.C: To allow pill fragments and food pieces to pass out without blocking the tube
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing any gag reflex during insertion

explanation: Small tubes easily clog with partially digested food or pill debris, rendering the wash ineffective; large-bore tubes provide a clear channel for thick debris to escape. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which lab value or vital sign must be checked regularly for patients on long-term corticosteroids?

options.A: Liver enzyme AST
options.B: Blood glucose levels
options.C: Red blood cell count
options.D: Serum creatinine

explanation: Correct! Steroids trigger the liver to release stored sugar, which often leads to high blood sugar levels that need close monitoring. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why does controlling rabies require teamwork between human health workers and vets?

options.A: The virus resides in animal reservoirs but causes fatal disease in humans
options.B: Veterinarians are trained to diagnose human psychiatric disorders
options.C: Animals can take human medications to cure their infections
options.D: Rabies is primarily spread through contaminated well water

explanation: Since dogs and wildlife are the main reservoir, we have to treat the animal population while also giving life-saving shots to exposed humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient is worried about her changing body after a hysterectomy. Which goal fits best in her care plan?

options.A: The patient will completely forget her anxiety within two hours
options.B: The nurse will make all decisions regarding her emotional care
options.C: The patient will verbalize feelings about body image changes before discharge
options.D: The patient will refuse to discuss her surgery with anyone

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is realistic, supportive, and lets the patient safely express her emotions regarding surgery. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for triggering the milk 'let-down' reflex when breastfeeding?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Wonderful! Oxytocin makes tiny muscles around the milk glands squeeze, pushing the milk forward for the baby. It's also the hormone of love and bonding! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h5)

question: How can we best describe public health surveillance?

options.A: A method for punishing clinics that lose patient files
options.B: A financial audit of private clinic expenditures
options.C: An ongoing system of collecting and analyzing health data
options.D: A one-time yearly census of hospital bed capacity

explanation: Think of surveillance as a continuous watch, not just a one-off check. We keep gathering and reviewing health data day in and day out to stay ahead of sickness! [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why do we routinely test the mother's urine for protein and acetone during active labour?

options.A: It proves whether the mother has taken her prescribed iron tablets
options.B: It helps identify pre-eclampsia and maternal starvation or dehydration
options.C: It measures the exact blood sugar level of the unborn baby
options.D: It determines the precise gestational age in weeks

explanation: Urine checks are quick lifesavers! Protein can point towards pre-eclampsia, while acetone tells you if the mother is running out of energy or getting dehydrated. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: When old skin flakes off after a minor scrape heals, which layer is mostly shedding?

options.A: Stratum corneum
options.B: Stratum basale
options.C: Stratum granulosum
options.D: Stratum spinosum

explanation: Spot on! The stratum corneum is our outermost layer made of tough, dead cells that naturally flake off over time. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant patient in her 8th week comes in with severe hyperthyroidism. Which medication should the nurse expect the doctor to order?

options.A: Lugol's iodine solution
options.B: Radioactive iodine-131
options.C: Propylthiouracil (PTU)
options.D: Methimazole

explanation: Spot on! PTU is the go-to medication during the first trimester of pregnancy to keep the baby safe from methimazole's risks. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h3)

question: Which sign points strongly to a wound infection after a skin biopsy?

options.A: A thin line of pink tissue along the suture line
options.B: Temporary numbness fading after the local anesthetic wears off
options.C: Spreading redness, warmth, and purulent drainage
options.D: Mild itching around the edges of the adhesive bandage

explanation: Redness that keeps spreading, feeling hot to the touch, pus (purulent drainage), and worsening pain are classic red flags that bacteria have moved in. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is a key characteristic of direct ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: It produces an inverted image that must be flipped mentally
options.B: It requires a heavy head-mounted light source worn by the examiner
options.C: It provides an upright, magnified view of a small retinal area
options.D: It gives a complete wide-angle view of the entire peripheral retina

explanation: Direct ophthalmoscopy uses a handy device to give an upright image magnified roughly 15 times, though it covers a narrower field than indirect methods. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of the living will movement?

options.A: To give doctors full authority over end-of-life care
options.B: To speed up the legal probate process for families
options.C: To help patients control their medical treatment choices ahead of time
options.D: To reduce overall hospital costs for elderly patients

explanation: The entire movement centers on letting individuals make their treatment preferences known before they lose the ability to speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why might a patient with severe carbon monoxide poisoning show a falsely normal or high oxygen saturation reading on a pulse oximeter?

options.A: Carbon monoxide makes the pulse rate extremely fast
options.B: Cold fingers stop the machine from recording low numbers
options.C: Bright lights in the room interfere with the infrared sensors
options.D: The device reads carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin just like oxygen

explanation: Standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between oxygen and carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin, leading to dangerously misleading high readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary mode of HIV transmission?

options.A: Unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
options.B: Sharing contaminated needles among drug users
options.C: Casual social contact like hugging and sharing utensils
options.D: Transmission from an infected mother to her baby during birth

explanation: HIV is not spread through everyday casual social contact, sweat, tears, saliva, or insect bites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why don't diaphragms and cervical caps protect very well against skin-to-skin STIs like HPV?

options.A: They leave the vaginal walls and external skin exposed
options.B: They allow semen to leak freely around the sides of the device
options.C: They dissolve too quickly when exposed to bodily fluids
options.D: They absorb viral particles and push them directly into the uterus

explanation: Correct! Because they only cover the cervix, surrounding skin and vaginal walls are still exposed to touch-based viruses. Great clinical insight! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h5)

question: How does the Drug Control Act directly affect daily nursing practice?

options.A: It decides which patients receive free medical care
options.B: It dictates the special handling rules for dangerous drugs
options.C: It sets the standard uniform code for hospital wards
options.D: It determines how many hours a nurse can work per week

explanation: The law sets clear rules on how nurses must store, give, and record potent medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h2)

question: What keeps a polyvalent nurse eager to keep learning on the job?

options.A: The desire to become a hospital administrator eventually
options.B: The need to maintain skills across many different medical fields
options.C: Pressure from hospital managers to reduce operating costs
options.D: Strict government laws requiring annual license renewals

explanation: Well done! Since they work in diverse units, polyvalent nurses always stay on their toes, updating their knowledge across multiple specialties. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: How does popular media often misrepresent sexual intercourse to teenagers?

options.A: As casual, glamorous, and rarely involving negative consequences
options.B: As an activity that requires strict medical supervision
options.C: As something that only occurs among older adults
options.D: As an event that always results in immediate health complications

explanation: Media portrayals frequently glamorize sex while omitting discussions of contraception, consent, and infections, creating unrealistic expectations. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h7)

question: A patient with coronary artery disease develops a sudden irregular heartbeat. What is the link between the disease and this rhythm change?

options.A: Coronary blockages directly destroy the sinoatrial node cells
options.B: Ischemia damages the heart's electrical conduction pathways
options.C: Narrowed arteries cause the heart to beat faster to compensate
options.D: Fatty plaques physically block electrical signals from traveling

explanation: When coronary arteries are narrowed, the heart muscle gets less oxygen (ischemia). Stressed, oxygen-starved heart cells have a hard time passing electrical signals smoothly, leading to irregular rhythms. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which diagnostic test directly checks the strength and status of a patient's immune system?

options.A: Urinalysis for protein
options.B: CD4+ T-cell count
options.C: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.D: Liver enzyme panel

explanation: Correct! The CD4+ count is our go-to test to see how many helper cells a patient has left to fight infections. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which bed position is best for instantly helping an out-of-breath patient expand their lungs?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: High-Fowler's position
options.C: Prone lying position
options.D: Flat supine position

explanation: Sitting upright in High-Fowler's position uses gravity to push abdominal organs downward, giving the lungs more room to fill with air. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: When you measure a patient's mid-upper arm circumference and body mass index, what kind of assessment are you doing?

options.A: Environmental factors
options.B: Biochemical data
options.C: Clinical signs
options.D: Anthropometric measurements

explanation: Don't let the big word scare you! 'Anthropometric' just means measuring physical body sizes like height, weight, and arm circumference to check nutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h2)

question: What is the medical term for menstrual bleeding that is unusually heavy or lasts too long?

options.A: Metrorrhagia
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia is the term for extra heavy or long periods. You will see this often in clinical practice when patients complain about soaking through pads too quickly. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following practices helps nurses avoid cultural stereotyping at the end of life?

options.A: Treating every patient from the exact same cultural background identically
options.B: Relying entirely on assumptions based on the patient's home country
options.C: Reading a textbook about world religions before every shift
options.D: Asking open questions about the patient's personal beliefs and traditions

explanation: Direct inquiry prevents stereotyping by letting patients define what their specific cultural and spiritual practices mean to them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why is it important for a patient to empty her bladder right before an MVA procedure?

options.A: To stop the kidneys from producing urine for the next several hours
options.B: To prevent accidental urine contamination of the surgical field
options.C: To test kidney function before giving any local anesthetic drugs
options.D: To make the pelvic exam and uterine positioning easier and less painful

explanation: A full bladder displaces the uterus, makes bimanual palpation difficult, and increases patient discomfort during speculum and instrument insertion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: Which public health intervention quickly protects young children against severe Vitamin A deficiency during immunisation drives?

options.A: Teaching mothers how to boil drinking water
options.B: Distribution of deworming tablets only
options.C: Periodic Vitamin A capsule supplementation
options.D: Enforcing mandatory school feeding programs

explanation: Spot on! Giving high-dose Vitamin A capsules during routine immunization outreach is a fast, effective way to keep kids protected. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h6)

question: What dangerous event happens when severe swelling inside the skull pushes brain tissue downward?

options.A: Brain herniation
options.B: Ventriculomegaly
options.C: Cortical atrophy
options.D: Neural regeneration

explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which chemical compound is commonly used for disinfecting blood spills on hard surfaces due to its quick action and low cost?

options.A: Liquid paraffin oil
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide cream
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Sodium hypochlorite, commonly known as bleach, is an affordable and effective disinfectant for clearing up blood spills. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is scolding or shouting at a returning defaulter a risky practice for a nurse?

options.A: It discourages the client from ever seeking care at that facility again
options.B: It violates international trade agreements
options.C: It instantly invalidates the chemical composition of oral pills
options.D: It causes immediate physical injury to the client's skin

explanation: Nobody wants to walk back into a place where they'll be judged. A welcoming attitude keeps our clinic doors open to those who need us most. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h4)

question: Which type of nerve fibers send those sharp, instant pain signals?

options.A: Ruffini fibers
options.B: Merkel fibers
options.C: C fibers
options.D: A-delta fibers

explanation: Brilliant! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin, which lets them rush electrical impulses quickly to cause that sharp first pain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the fastest and preferred energy source for your brain and nerves?

options.A: Glucose from carbohydrates
options.B: Fatty acids from dietary lipids
options.C: Amino acids from proteins
options.D: Vitamins from fresh fruit

explanation: Think of carbohydrates as premium fuel! They quickly break down into glucose, which is the brain's absolute favorite energy source. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h2)

question: What are the two main jobs of the external male reproductive organs?

options.A: Hormone production and digestion
options.B: Sperm maturation and temperature regulation
options.C: Blood filtration and fluid balance
options.D: Urine elimination and sexual reproduction

explanation: You've got it! The penis and urethra pull double duty: they help pass out urine from the bladder and also help deliver sperm during reproduction. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the biggest safety hazard to watch out for during steam tent therapy?

options.A: Hypertensive crisis
options.B: Sudden hypoglycemia
options.C: Scald burns
options.D: Severe hypothermia

explanation: Correct! Because boiling water and hot steam are involved, burn prevention is always a top priority. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is a common dietary trap patients fall into when starting a low-fat diet?

options.A: Eating too many leafy green vegetables every day
options.B: Consuming too much lean skinless chicken breast
options.C: Replacing healthy fats with large amounts of sugary foods
options.D: Drinking excessive amounts of plain filtered water

explanation: When foods lose their fat content, they can taste bland. Patients often make the mistake of loading up on sweets and refined carbs to compensate, which messes with blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h5)

question: What type of mask must nurses wear when walking into an active TB patient's room?

options.A: Standard paper surgical mask for fluid splashes
options.B: Particulate respirator such as an N95 mask
options.C: Cloth face covering made from thick cotton fabric
options.D: Plastic face shield with no respiratory filter

explanation: Because TB travels on tiny air particles, ordinary surgical masks won't cut it. An N95 respirator keeps healthcare workers safe! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h6)

question: What life-threatening emergency can happen if a patient stops taking long-term steroids all of a sudden?

options.A: Heart attack
options.B: Malignant hypertension
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Addisonian crisis

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping steroids abruptly when the adrenal glands are inactive throws the body into a dangerous crash called an addisonian crisis. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is a BAD risk management practice for a staff nurse?

options.A: Falsifying patient charts to hide a missed medication dose
options.B: Practicing strictly within the established scope of licensure
options.C: Maintaining clear and accurate clinical documentation
options.D: Following hospital safety protocols and clinical guidelines

explanation: Falsifying records is dishonest, illegal, and will instantly multiply your legal trouble if things go wrong. Always document honestly! [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h7)

question: Why do we place a footrest or pillow at the bottom of a cardiac bed?

options.A: To prevent the patient from sliding downward while in a sitting position
options.B: To provide a stable surface for the patient to attach leg exercise bands
options.C: To improve blood circulation directly to the lower extremities
options.D: To stop the mattress from sagging in the middle of the frame

explanation: You nailed it! Because the bed is propped up high, gravity tries to pull the patient down. The footrest keeps them comfortably in place. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do nurses look at both "typical use" and "perfect use" when talking about birth control?

options.A: Perfect use is only measured during laboratory animal testing phases
options.B: Typical use measures how long the drug remains active in the liver
options.C: Typical use accounts for real-world human error like missed doses
options.D: Perfect use calculates the exact financial cost of the medication

explanation: Nobody's perfect! Real-world or "typical use" failure rates reflect how people actually take drugs day-to-day—like forgetting a pill or taking an injection a bit late. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h1)

question: A patient reports soaking three large sanitary pads in less than an hour after an abortion. What should you as a nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge the patient home with instructions to return in one week.
options.B: Advise the patient to take a hot bath and rest in bed.
options.C: Report the heavy bleeding to the clinician and assess vital signs.
options.D: Tell the patient this is a completely normal post-procedure finding.

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour is a red flag for hemorrhage! Your immediate nursing priority is to check her vital signs and notify the doctor right away. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h6)

question: Why is it important to include family members in dietary education for a patient requiring a low salt diet?

options.A: Family members are the ones who administer oral medications at home
options.B: Family members are legally responsible for paying hospital medical bills
options.C: Family members must also follow the exact same medical diagnosis
options.D: Family members usually prepare the meals and must support the dietary changes

explanation: In many homes, cooking is shared or done by someone other than the patient, so family buy-in ensures the right food gets cooked. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h7)

question: What is the main goal of taking anti-seizure medications?

options.A: To prevent future seizures by stabilizing brain activity
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying cause of epilepsy
options.C: To increase the speed of brain electrical signals
options.D: To immediately stop pain during a headache

explanation: These meds act like a steady anchor for the brain, calming down hyperactive nerve cells so seizures don't catch the patient off guard. You've got this concept down! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way to handle cultural diversity in learning?

options.A: Understanding that cultural backgrounds shape views on health and authority
options.B: Assuming every student learns and communicates in the exact same way
options.C: Recognizing diverse viewpoints to enrich classroom discussions
options.D: Creating a space where different communication styles are respected

explanation: Remember, we are all unique! Educators must embrace student diversity rather than expecting everyone to learn through a single mold. [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h5)

question: Why must nurse supervisors make sure staff stay strictly within their scope of practice?

options.A: To prevent professional misconduct and protect patient safety
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of running the hospital ward
options.C: To make sure doctors do not have to do any ward work
options.D: To speed up the promotion process for junior nurses

explanation: Knowing your scope keeps patients safe from harm and protects you legally from stepping outside your training. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: What should you do when a clear-headed home care patient refuses a necessary treatment?

options.A: Ask family members to pressure the patient into agreeing
options.B: Educate on the risks, respect the choice, and document the refusal
options.C: Immediately discharge the patient from the home care agency
options.D: Administer the treatment anyway to prevent complications

explanation: Well done! Always give them the facts so they understand the risks, but remember: competent adults have the final say over their own bodies. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h3)

question: How might a severely distressed mum in labour act behaviorally?

options.A: A calm and deeply sleeping demeanor
options.B: Complete willingness to ambulate alone
options.C: A steady focus on hospital paperwork
options.D: Extreme agitation or sudden withdrawal

explanation: Distress wears different faces: some mums show it through loud panic and restlessness, while others go quiet and completely withdraw. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h4)

question: Which two types of viral hepatitis currently have safe, effective vaccines available?

options.A: Hepatitis A and C
options.B: Hepatitis B and E
options.C: Hepatitis C and D
options.D: Hepatitis A and B

explanation: Brilliant! We have reliable vaccines ready to protect people from both Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B infections. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h8)

question: Why is it so important to keep pauses in chest compressions as short as possible when using an AED?

options.A: Pauses reduce blood flow to the heart and brain, lowering survival rates.
options.B: Pauses allow the patient's body temperature to drop too quickly.
options.C: Pauses confuse the AED computer and prevent rhythm analysis.

question: What is the primary role of the cerebellum in the nervous system?

question: What is the main goal that drives voluntary health agencies?

question: A cancer patient says food smells too strong and tastes like metal. What is a helpful nursing tip?

options.D: Recommend adding extra iron supplements to every meal

question: What is the correct action a nurse should take before applying a new dose of a topical skin cream?

question: Why isn't just coming into contact with an infectious germ always enough to make someone sick?
